VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY:
- A = ∅: f is the empty function, injective; the only subsets are S=T=∅; all equalities hold trivially; proof steps with existential quantifiers over ∅ are vacuously true or correctly handled.
- S = ∅ (or T = ∅): f[∅] = ∅; unions/intersections/differences with ∅ behave as required; the general inclusions hold, and the reverse inclusions under injectivity hold vacuously where needed.
- f injective with S ∩ T = ∅: then f[S] ∩ f[T] = ∅, so equality in (ii) holds; step 2.4(ii) correctly covers the case where the premise is false.
- f non-injective with a,a'∈A, a≠a', f(a)=f(a'): S={a}, T={a'} yields S∩T=∅, f[S∩T]=∅, f[S]∩f[T]={f(a)}≠∅; step 2.5 correctly shows the inclusion in (ii) is proper.
- S = T: S∩T=S, S\T=∅; the equalities hold (both sides equal f[S] or ∅); proof steps remain valid.
- S\T = ∅ (i.e. S ⊆ T): then f[S\T] = ∅; the general inclusion f[S]\f[T] ⊆ ∅ forces equality ∅; under injectivity the reverse inclusion also holds; no defect.
- f constant, non-injective: the counterexample S,T singleton works as above; the general inclusions hold.
